analysis:
This batch has only documentation and changelog changes: changelog.d/glm-variable-frame-rate-video.md (new) and docs/architecture/inference.md (hunks at head lines ~810-813 and ~829). No executable source is supplied, so the actual GLM5NextProcessor change is not visible here.

The docs say GLM-5.3-Flash video_url clips with a variable frame rate are now indexed in presentation order and timed at i / nominalFrameRate, instead of being refused with 400 invalid_media. The unchanged 2 FPS sampler, the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes) and the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap are documented as still applying.

Security relevance is limited to the TB-007 provider inference engine and TB-003 (operator versus process) media-ingest availability surface. The previously documented rejection of variable-frame-rate video is removed. The likely threat is a hostile consumer-supplied video causing memory or CPU exhaustion (DoS). The documentation states that the decode caps stay in place. Whether they actually hold depends on the Swift implementation, which is not in this batch. If the implementation iterates every frame to compute indices, a clip with a huge frame count or a misleading nominalFrameRate could bypass any frame-count bound. The documentation does not state such a bound for this path, unlike the Nemotron path's maximumSourceFrames. Reviewers of the code diff should check: frame-count and duration bounds before decoding, nominalFrameRate of zero or NaN handling, and the decode-time allowance.

Media requests remain excluded from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), so T-041 cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing is unaffected. The docs change does not alter encryption, attestation, the coordinator boundary or any threat-model assumption. No finding is raised from documentation alone; the implementation diff needs review for the DoS bounds above.
